19	## 1. The product in one page
20	
21	BMW product managers (PMs) decide which customer requirements go into the next generation of a vehicle (G60 = 5 Series, F70 = 1 Series, G70 = 7 Series). The app turns heterogeneous evidence into traceable, prioritized requirements, with the PM deciding at every step.
22	
23	**Chain:** `Signal → Case → Requirement → Vehicle plan → Codebeamer`
24	
25	| Concept | Meaning | Frontend entity | Backend table |
26	|---|---|---|---|
27	| **Signal** | One piece of evidence with its source: a BMW verbatim, a study row, a web review, a competitor fact | `Signal` | `signal` (+ `source_record`) |
28	| **Case** | A customer **problem**, built from a group of signals on one topic. Has an importance score, **no cost** | `Case` | `case_item` + `case_vehicle` (per line) + `case_score` |
29	| **Requirement** | What BMW builds to solve a confirmed case: SMART text, measurable targets, release, rough cost | `Requirement` | `requirement` |
30	| **Vehicle plan** | Requirements of a series grouped by car area, next to today's equipment; exported to Codebeamer | `VehiclePlan` / `PlannedFeature` | (none; `vehicle_feature` holds today's equipment) |
31	
32	**Non-negotiable rules (both codebases agree):**
33	1. **AI proposes, PM decides.** The AI never edits directly: it returns proposals (frontend `Proposal`, backend `chat_message.proposed_diff`) that a person accepts or rejects.
34	2. **Every human decision has a reason** and every change writes an **append-only audit event** (who or what, when, before/after, rationale).
35	3. **Traceability:** every requirement links back to its case, the case to its signals, signals to their source quote.
36	4. **Fixed taxonomy:** 11 car areas, 219 topics, 11 aspect groups (`taxonomy/taxonomy.json`). Agents classify into it; they never invent categories (Thomas's feedback).
37	5. **Customer-facing requirements only:** regulatory, engineering specs and pricing are out of scope.
38	6. **Score formula is explainable:** case score = weighted mean of factors (0..1); requirement rank = case score × cost multiplier (S/M/L).
39	
40	**Personas (frontend demo, synthetic):** Lena Hofmann (PM 5 Series, rest of world), Wei Zhang (PM 5 Series, China), Jonas Berger (cross-series attribute PM, operating concept / HMI, "Baukasten"), Katrin Maier (head of product line: signs off, resolves escalations), Sofia Rossi (PM 1 Series), Daniel Okafor (PM 7 Series).

67	## 3. How the frontend works (architecture)
68	
69	### 3.1 Contract-first
70	- Every endpoint is declared once in `web/src/contracts/api.ts` (`endpoints` object: method, path, query, body, response as Zod schemas). Entities in `entities.ts`, vocabularies in `enums.ts`, UI labels in `labels.ts`.
71	- `npm run export-contract` writes `contracts/openapi.yaml` and `contracts/schemas/*.json`.
72	- `npm run contract-test` (`API_BASE=…`) calls every endpoint against a running server, validates every response with Zod, and walks the demo storyline. **Any data source behind the UI must pass it** (the storyline uses seeded IDs such as `CASE-G60-0001`, so it needs parametrizing for real data).
73	
74	### 3.2 Data access
75	- The UI never imports `src/mock`. It calls `api(name, { params, query, body })` from `src/lib/api/client.ts`, or the hooks `useApi(name, opts)` / `useApiMutation(name)` from `src/lib/api/hooks.ts`.
76	- Base URL: `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` (default `/api` = the mock route).
77	- **Every successful mutation invalidates every query** (`qc.invalidateQueries()`): simple and always consistent, fine for demo-sized data. With 13,000 real signals some screens will need pagination (section 9).
78	- Errors: the client expects `{ error: string, issues? }` and an HTTP status; it throws `ApiRequestError`, shown as a toast.
79	
80	### 3.3 Auth (demo)
81	- `/login` lists users (`GET /users`); picking one sets the cookie `rs_user` (`src/lib/session.ts`). The client sends it as header `x-user-id`. The mock route resolves the user from its store (`u-lena`, `u-wei`, `u-jonas`, `u-katrin`, `u-sofia`, `u-daniel`).
82	
83	### 3.4 The mock backend
84	- `route.ts` matches method + path against the contract, parses query/body with Zod, calls `handlers[name]({ params, query, body, user })`, validates the response in dev, maps `ApiError(status)` to JSON errors.
85	- `src/mock/store.ts`: one in-memory `Dataset` (shape = `Dataset` entity) cloned from `fixtures/seed.json`; `audit()`, `notify()`, `nextId()`, `now()`; `POST /admin/reset` restores the seed. Quality checks live in a side map (`checks()`).
86	- `src/mock/handlers.ts`: one function per endpoint, holding the business rules (section 6).
87	- `src/mock/scoring.ts`: reference scorer. `src/mock/ai/*`: scripted AI (chat intents, drafts, meeting-note extraction, quality check, segments); `ai/live.ts` optionally calls Claude when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set (free-form chat, quality-check LLM pass, segment summary). The backend uses OpenAI; after integration the chat should go to the backend RAG agent.
88	- Seed: `npm run seed` rebuilds `seed.json` from the real CSVs in `docs/02-data/processed/` (404 selected verbatims, study rows, 2030 sales) plus authored synthetic content (people, web signals, competitor facts, decisions, requirements, audit history). Synthetic objects carry `synthetic: true` and the UI tags them.

220	## 6. Business logic implemented in the frontend mock
221	
222	These rules live in `web/src/mock/handlers.ts` and `web/src/mock/ai/*`. Whatever replaces the mock must keep them (in the backend, the adapter or the sidecar).
223	
224	### 6.1 Permissions
225	- Only the case **owner or a co-owner** (or the head) changes a case; everyone can read, comment, watch, escalate. Only the requirement owner (or head) edits it.
226	- **Head of product line** (`role = head`) sends back, signs off, resolves escalations, edits the brand profile and default weight profiles.
227	- Series PMs (plan `ownerIds`) edit the vehicle plan.
228	
229	### 6.2 Case lifecycle (frontend)
230	- States: `observed → new → investigating → awaiting_answers → ready → decided`. Actions `open`, `start`, `await`, `ready`, `reopen` move the state; every move needs a rationale.
231	- Deciding sets `state = decided` and an **outcome**: `confirm` (drafts requirements via the requirement agent if none exist), `refer` (to another PM: creates a `Referral`, the receiver becomes a watcher and is notified), `innovation` (adds to the pool with a horizon and the PM's pitch), `park`, `reject`, `merge` (moves signals into the target, recomputes its figures, notifies the target owner).
232	- `refer` with `escalate: true` creates an **escalation** to the head instead (anyone involved may escalate, e.g. China vs. rest-of-world conflict).
233	- Every decision is prepended to the case page's "Decision log" and audited.
234	- Referral decisions: `accept` creates a **linked case** in the receiver's workspace (`originCaseId`), `decline` puts the source case back to `ready`, `escalate` hands it to the head, `resolve` (head) records a resolution (one market, market variant, keep both, take over, return) in the case context and decision log.
235	
236	### 6.3 Requirement lifecycle (frontend)
237	`draft → in_discussion → pm_approved → signed_off → planned → exported`, plus `rejected` (restore → `draft`).
238	- `approve` (owner, from draft or in discussion) notifies the head with a sign-off request; the open quality-check issues are recorded in the audit event (section 6.9).
239	- `send_back` (head, from pm_approved) → `in_discussion` with `sentBackReason`, owner notified.
240	- `sign_off` (head, from pm_approved) → owner notified.
241	- `plan` (owner/head, from signed_off) links or creates a `PlannedFeature` in the series plan.
242	- `export` (from planned); the Codebeamer export also moves every planned requirement to `exported`.
243	- IDs: `REQ-<series>-NNNN`, China variants `REQ-<series>-CN-NNNN`.
244	
245	### 6.4 Scoring (reference, `mock/scoring.ts`)
246	- Factors (all 0..1): `customers`, `severity`, `satisfaction_gap`, `competitor_gap`, `market_volume`, `regression`, `trend`, `brand_fit`.
247	- `case score = Σ w_f · factor_f / Σ w_f` (no cost). `requirement score = case score × costMultiplier[size]`.
248	- Manual ranks (with reason) win over the computed order. Observed, rejected and merged cases are not ranked.
249	- `previewScores` re-ranks with unsaved weights; the UI shows "moved because…" and a robustness column (stays in the top 5 under every profile).
250	- `customers` is recomputed from the case's signals: `log10(1 + n) / log10(61)`.
251	
252	### 6.5 AI assistant (`mock/ai/chat.ts`, scripted unless a key is set)
253	Intent by message text; every answer cites evidence as `[SIGNAL-ID]`, and every change is a proposal:
254	- "research …" → mock research run adds two synthetic web signals to the case (audited as `agent:researcher`).
255	- "draft a SMART requirement" → `new_requirement` proposal(s) from `ai/drafts.ts`.
256	- "what should I ask engineering/finance" → `new_question` proposals.
257	- "why is this ranked so high", "compare the markets", "what do competitors offer", "argument sheet", "set the target to …" (field proposal) → cited answers.
258	- Free-form questions go to the live LLM when available (context: case, figures, up to 40 signals, page, requirement).
259	- `savePmContext` stores the PM's market focus, cost sensitivity, positioning, timing and note in the case context, then the assistant posts 1 to 2 follow-up questions the data cannot answer (market mismatch, platform change vs. LCI, paid option vs. standard, match/beat competitors).
260	- `addMeetingNote` (`ai/notes.ts`) extracts answers to open questions, field updates and decision-log entries from pasted notes as proposals.
261	- Proposal kinds: `field`, `body`, `question_answer`, `new_question`, `new_requirement`. Accepting applies the change, logs a context entry and an audit event.
262	
263	### 6.6 Monitoring and refresh
264	- `refresh` runs once over a pool of authored web findings: new signals attach to their case, owners and watchers are notified, a competitor fact with a metric raises an **alert** ("raises the bar") on the case; a second run finds nothing (dedupe by URL and content hash). An `AgentRun` is recorded.
265	- `resolveAlert`: dismiss, or `rework` (requirement back to in_discussion, case back to investigating).
266	
267	### 6.7 Vehicle plan and export
268	- The plan lists features per car area with today's availability (standard/optional/absent/removed), action (keep/new/improve/remove), release, protected flag and linked requirements.
269	- Codebeamer CSV columns: ID, Summary, Description, Category, Market, Release, Priority, Score, Evidence level, Metrics, Acceptance criteria, Assumptions, Cost size, Cost band, Linked case, Linked findings, Rationale, Status. Sorted by rank under the user's weight profile.
270	
271	### 6.8 Engineering deck (`requirementDeck` + `web/src/lib/deck.ts`)
272	Signed-off, planned and exported requirements of a series, sorted by rank. Per slide: SMART text and metrics, top 3 BMW complaint quotes (not likes), score breakdown (factor value × normalized weight), competitor gap, last 5 decisions (requirement and case), open quality issues. Rendered client-side with `pptxgenjs`. Easy to rebuild on real data: it only needs requirement, case factors + weights, case signals and decisions.
273	
274	### 6.9 Quality check (`mock/ai/quality.ts`)
275	Runs automatically after drafting and every edit, and on demand. Warns, never blocks; approving lists the open issues and requires a reason.
276	- `vague_word` (title, description, acceptance criteria: "improved", "better", "user-friendly", "intuitive", "seamless", …; red if no metric has a numeric target).
277	- `missing_scope` (scope global while > 80 % of the case's verbatims come from one market; China scope with < 3 Chinese verbatims).
278	- `out_of_scope` (homologation, type approval, UN-R, ISO 26262, emissions, crash test, ECU, CAN bus, supplier, part number, price/pricing, business case) — red.
279	- `duplicate` (≥ 30 % word overlap with a live requirement of the same series, red) / `baukasten` (same in another series, or the case spans several series, amber, suggests the cross-series PM).
280	- `conflict` (same metric question with another target in the same car area; or relies on a feature the plan removes).
281	- Optional LLM pass adds issues of the same kinds (strict JSON, related IDs validated).
282	Portable as-is: inputs are a requirement, its case figures, all requirements and the plan. Could later move to Python next to `requirements/service.py`.
283	
284	### 6.10 Ask the segment (`mock/ai/segment.ts`)
285	- Segments = markets of the case (+ market × powertrain with ≥ 3 verbatims), counted **only from real BMW verbatims** (no synthetic, no web).
286	- With verbatims: counts by kind + 3 to 5 strongest quotes, cited. Live LLM gets only that segment's quotes and must summarize in the third person; citations not in the set are dropped.
287	- Without verbatims: "No evidence for China owners", the closest segment with data, and a `new_question` proposal to the market PM. Never a guess.
288	- On real data: segments come from `GET /signals?case_id=…` filtered by `evidence_role = bmw_customer` (or `source_id = bmw_feedback`), grouped by `market` and `powertrain`.
289

430	## 9. Gotchas
431	
432	- **Scale.** The mock has 28 cases and ~500 signals; the backend has 1,206 cases (376 opened by rule per line pair), ~13,000 valid signals. The case board should show `open` + `confirmed` by default (backend default) and the Sankey needs aggregated counts (sources × car areas × cases) rather than every signal: add an aggregate endpoint or compute from `GET /cases?profile_id` (per-case `source_types`, `markets`, `distinct_customers`).
433	- **"Invalidate everything after a mutation"** (`hooks.ts`) re-fetches all active queries; with real data, narrow it to the affected keys if screens get slow.
434	- **Stale saves:** backend returns 409 when `expected_version` is old; the UI must reload the page instead of overwriting.
435	- **Per-vehicle actions:** every case action on the backend needs the vehicle (`/vehicles/{vehicle}/…`). Use the persona's config vehicle; Baukasten cases appear for several lines and each line decides separately.
436	- **Permissions differ:** backend lets any PM of one of the case's lines act; the frontend uses owner/co-owners. Until owners exist in the backend, check ownership in the adapter (sidecar) before calling.
437	- **Market labels:** `Rest of World` has spaces; URL-encode it in query strings.
438	- **Citations:** the UI's markdown turns `[ID]` into clickable links that open the signal on the case page. Backend signal ids are uuids, and the case page must be able to find them (the signals of the case must be loaded with the same ids).

566	    """What-if ranking for unsaved weights, from the stored factor values of the profile
567	    (score = brand multiplier x sum(weight x factor) / sum(weight)). Nothing is stored."""
568	    profile = c.execute("select * from weight_profile where id = %s", (body.profile_id,)).fetchone()
569	    if profile is None:

571	    unknown = set(body.weights) - set(score.FACTORS)
572	    if unknown:
573	        raise HTTPException(422, f"unknown factors {sorted(unknown)}")
574	    weights = score.normalize_weights({**profile["case_weights"], **body.weights})
575	    cases = []
576	    for r in rank.case_board(c, body.profile_id):
577	        factors = r["factors"] or {}
578	        contributions = {f: round(float(factors.get(f, {}).get("normalized") or 0) * w, 4)
579	                         for f, w in weights.items()}
580	        cases.append({"case_id": r["id"], "manual_rank": r["manual_rank"], "contributions": contributions,
581	                      "score": round(sum(contributions.values()) * float(r["brand_multiplier"] or 0.8), 4)})
582	    manual = sorted((x for x in cases if x["manual_rank"] is not None), key=lambda x: x["manual_rank"])
583	    auto = sorted((x for x in cases if x["manual_rank"] is None), key=lambda x: -x["score"])
584	    for i, x in enumerate(manual + auto, start=1):
585	        x["rank"] = i
586	    by_case = {x["case_id"]: x["score"] for x in cases}
587	    reqs = [{"requirement_id": r["id"],
588	             "score": rank.requirement_rank(by_case.get(r["case_id"]), r["cost_size"], profile["cost_multipliers"]) or 0}
589	            for r in service.board(c, body.profile_id, statuses=service.LIVE)]
590	    for i, r in enumerate(sorted(reqs, key=lambda r: -r["score"]), start=1):
591	        r["rank"] = i
592	    return {"profile_id": body.profile_id, "weights": weights, "cases": manual + auto, "requirements": reqs}

    _refresh(c, case_id)

    from app.cases import pipeline

    require_pm(user, vehicle)

"""Read models for the UI: case board with filters, overview map, case page."""

from __future__ import annotations

from app.scoring.rank import case_board

STATES = ("observed", "open", "confirmed", "rejected")
# What the PM workspace shows on a case card: the AI-written card texts and the PM's work for the line.
WORK_COLUMNS = ("short_title", "summary", "highlights", "case_type", "change_depth", "brand_fit_reason",
                "brand_fit_source", "brand_fit_confirmed_by", "body_version", "created_at", "created_by",
                "updated_at", "workflow", "outcome", "outcome_note", "owner_id", "co_owner_ids", "watcher_ids",
                "scope")


def board(conn, profile_id, *, states=("open", "confirmed"), car_area: str | None = None,
          release_fit: str | None = None, market: str | None = None, source_type: str | None = None,
          source_id: str | None = None, aspect_group: str | None = None, conflict_only: bool = False,
          q: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """The ranked board of one weight profile (= vehicle + market), with the end filters
    market, car area, state, source type and release fit. Ranks are the board ranks
    before filtering, so a filtered view keeps each case's place."""
    rows = case_board(conn, profile_id, states=states)
    if not rows:
        return rows
    ids = [r["id"] for r in rows]
    meta = {m["id"]: m for m in conn.execute(
        "select c.id, c.aspect_group, c.scope_tag, f.topic_id, f.name as topic, f.car_area,"
        " c.figures->'by_vehicle' as by_vehicle, c.figures->'source_types' as source_types,"
        " c.figures->'sources' as sources, (c.figures->>'signals')::int as signals"
        " from case_item c join feature f on f.id = c.feature_id where c.id = any(%s)", (ids,)).fetchall()}
    others: dict[str, list] = {}
    for o in conn.execute("select case_id, vehicle from case_vehicle where case_id = any(%s) order by vehicle",
                          (ids,)).fetchall():
        others.setdefault(o["case_id"], []).append(o["vehicle"])
    vehicle = rows[0]["vehicle"]
    others = {k: [v for v in vs if v != vehicle] for k, vs in others.items()}
    requirements: dict[str, list] = {}
    for req in conn.execute("select id, case_id from requirement where case_id = any(%s) and vehicle = %s"
                            " and status <> 'deleted' order by id", (ids, vehicle)).fetchall():
        requirements.setdefault(req["case_id"], []).append(req["id"])
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        m = meta[r["id"]]
        vf = (m["by_vehicle"] or {}).get(r["vehicle"], {})
        markets = vf.get("markets", {})
        if car_area and m["car_area"] != car_area:
            continue
        if aspect_group and m["aspect_group"] != aspect_group:
            continue
        if release_fit and r["release_fit"] != release_fit:
            continue
        if market and not markets.get(market, {}).get("customers"):
            continue
        if source_type and not (m["source_types"] or {}).get(source_type):
            continue
        if source_id and not (m["sources"] or {}).get(source_id):
            continue
        if conflict_only and not r["market_conflict"]:
            continue
        if q and q.lower() not in (r["title"] or "").lower() and q.lower() not in m["topic"].lower():
            continue
        out.append({
            **{k: r[k] for k in ("rank", "id", "title", "vehicle", "state", "score", "rationale", "previous_score",
                                 "score_moved", "manual_rank", "manual_rank_reason", "release_fit", "market_conflict",
                                 "flag_new_evidence", "brand_fit", "segment", *WORK_COLUMNS)},
            "factors": {f: v.get("normalized") for f, v in (r["factors"] or {}).items()},
            "contributions": {f: v.get("contribution") for f, v in (r["factors"] or {}).items()},
            "other_vehicles": others.get(r["id"], []),
            "requirement_ids": requirements.get(r["id"], []),
            "markets_full": markets,
            "equipment": vf.get("equipment", {}),
            "competitor_offers": vf.get("competitor_offers", []),
            "trend_signals": vf.get("trend_signals", 0),
            "study": vf.get("study", []),
            "signals": m["signals"],
            "topic_id": m["topic_id"], "topic": m["topic"], "car_area": m["car_area"],
            "aspect_group": m["aspect_group"], "scope_tag": m["scope_tag"],
            "distinct_customers": vf.get("distinct_customers", 0),
            "markets": {k: {"customers": v.get("customers", 0), "negative_share": v.get("negative_share")}
                        for k, v in markets.items()},
            "competitor_signals": vf.get("competitor_evidence", {}).get("signals", 0),
            "source_types": m["source_types"] or {},
        })
    return out


def overview(conn, vehicle: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Overview map: every case of a line (observed included) counted per car area and state."""
    rows = conn.execute(
        "select f.car_area, cv.state, count(*) as cases,"
        " sum(coalesce((c.figures->'by_vehicle'->%s->>'distinct_customers')::int, 0)) as customers"
        " from case_vehicle cv join case_item c on c.id = cv.case_id join feature f on f.id = c.feature_id"
        " where cv.vehicle = %s group by 1, 2 order by 1, 2", (vehicle, vehicle)).fetchall()
    areas: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for r in rows:
        a = areas.setdefault(r["car_area"] or "unknown", {"car_area": r["car_area"], "states": {}, "customers": 0})
        a["states"][r["state"]] = r["cases"]
        a["customers"] += int(r["customers"] or 0)
    return sorted(areas.values(), key=lambda a: -a["customers"])


def page(conn, case_id: str) -> dict | None:
    case = conn.execute(
        "select c.*, f.topic_id, f.name as topic, f.car_area from case_item c join feature f on f.id = c.feature_id"
        " where c.id = %s", (case_id,)).fetchone()
    if case is None:
        return None
    case.pop("embedding", None)
    case["vehicles"] = conn.execute("select * from case_vehicle where case_id = %s order by vehicle",
                                    (case_id,)).fetchall()
    case["lineage"] = conn.execute(
        "select from_case, to_case, op, actor, rationale, created_at from case_lineage"
        " where from_case = %s or to_case = %s order by created_at", (case_id, case_id)).fetchall()
    case["scores"] = conn.execute(
        "select s.weight_profile_id, p.name as profile, c.id as config_id, c.vehicle, c.market, s.score,"
        " s.brand_multiplier, s.factors, s.rationale, s.computed_at from case_score_current s"
        " join weight_profile p on p.id = s.weight_profile_id join config c on c.id = p.config_id"
        " where s.case_id = %s order by c.vehicle, c.market, p.name", (case_id,)).fetchall()
    case["requirements"] = conn.execute(
        "select id, vehicle, market, title, status from requirement where case_id = %s order by id",
        (case_id,)).fetchall()
    case["decisions"] = conn.execute(
        "select vehicle, actor, action, rationale, created_at from decision where object_type = 'case'"
        " and object_id = %s order by created_at desc limit 50", (case_id,)).fetchall()
    # The PM's work on the case: context, questions, notes, hand-overs, flags, proposals.
    rids = [r["id"] for r in case["requirements"]]
    case["stances"] = conn.execute("select * from case_stance where case_id = %s order by updated_at",
                                   (case_id,)).fetchall()
    case["questions"] = conn.execute(
        "select * from open_question where (object_type = 'case' and object_id = %s)"
        " or (object_type = 'requirement' and object_id = any(%s)) order by created_at", (case_id, rids)).fetchall()
    case["meeting_notes"] = conn.execute("select * from meeting_note where case_id = %s order by created_at",
                                         (case_id,)).fetchall()
    case["referrals"] = conn.execute("select * from referral where case_id = %s order by created_at desc",
                                     (case_id,)).fetchall()
    case["alerts"] = conn.execute("select * from alert where case_id = %s or requirement_id = any(%s)"
                                  " order by created_at desc", (case_id, rids)).fetchall()
    case["proposals"] = conn.execute(
        "select * from proposal where (object_type = 'case' and object_id = %s)"
        " or (object_type = 'requirement' and object_id = any(%s)) order by created_at", (case_id, rids)).fetchall()
    case["innovation"] = conn.execute("select * from innovation_item where case_id = %s", (case_id,)).fetchone()
    return case


def signals(conn, *, case_id: str | None = None, vehicle: str | None = None, market: str | None = None,
            kind: str | None = None, evidence_role: str | None = None, source_id: str | None = None,
            content_type: str | None = None, car_area: str | None = None, topic_id: str | None = None,
            validation: str = "valid", unassigned: bool = False, q: str | None = None, limit: int = 50,
            offset: int = 0) -> dict:
    where, params = ["s.validation = %s"], [validation]
    if unassigned:
        where.append("s.case_id is null")
    if q:
        where.append("(s.summary ilike %s or s.quote ilike %s)")
        params += [f"%{q}%", f"%{q}%"]
    for col, val in (("s.case_id", case_id), ("s.vehicle", vehicle), ("s.market", market), ("s.kind", kind),
                     ("s.evidence_role", evidence_role), ("r.source_id", source_id),
                     ("r.content_type", content_type), ("f.topic_id", topic_id)):
        if val:
            where.append(f"{col} = %s")
            params.append(val)
    if car_area:
        where.append("%s = any(s.car_area)")
        params.append(car_area)
    sql_where = " and ".join(where)
    total = conn.execute(
        "select count(*) n from signal s join source_record r using (record_id) left join feature f"
        f" on f.id = s.feature_id where {sql_where}", params).fetchone()["n"]
    rows = conn.execute(
        "select s.id, s.record_id, s.case_id, s.kind, s.severity, s.summary, s.quote, s.quote_en, s.market,"
        " s.vehicle, s.chassis_code, s.vehicle_role, s.evidence_role, s.powertrain, s.reach, s.reach_unit,"
        " s.aspect_group, s.car_area, s.classified_by, s.scope_tag, s.published_at, f.topic_id, f.name as topic,"
        " s.market_basis, s.feature_hint, s.validation, s.created_at,"
        " r.source_id, r.content_type, r.category, r.url, r.title as record_title, r.fetched_at, r.country,"
        " r.language, sr.name as source_name, co.brand || ' ' || co.model as competitor,"
        " case when d.record_id is null then null else jsonb_build_object('name', d.metric, 'value', d.value,"
        " 'unit', d.unit, 'period', d.period) end as metric"
        " from signal s join source_record r using (record_id) left join feature f on f.id = s.feature_id"
        " left join source_registry sr on sr.source_id = r.source_id"
        " left join competitor co on co.id = s.competitor_id"
        " left join data_record d on d.record_id = s.data_record_id and d.value is not null"
        f" where {sql_where} order by s.published_at desc nulls last, s.id limit %s offset %s",
        [*params, limit, offset]).fetchall()
    return {"total": total, "items": rows}

content.text:
The merged UI is consistent and correctly wired on the demo (mock) data, but several of the features this merge added are broken or silently do nothing on the real backend. Nothing was changed in the repo; the live-backend findings come from reading the adapter against the FastAPI routes, not from running it (I did not start the backend).

**What I reviewed:** `origin/main` at `1dd1db6` (PR #10, `ui/awesomic-restyle`), from an exported copy. Your local `main` is 35 commits behind it (still at PR #6). During the review the checkout switched to `feature/web-import-signals` with uncommitted edits in `backend/app/fetch/`, so another session is active in this folder; I left it alone and only ran `git fetch`.

## What holds
- **Coverage:** all 76 contract endpoints have a mock handler and an adapter handler, and every adapter call targets a backend route that exists. The UI calls nothing outside the contract.
- **Static checks:** lint and the 8 mapping tests pass; typecheck is clean apart from two `LayoutProps` errors, which come from Next's generated types missing in my exported copy.
- **Mock behaviour:** the contract-test storyline passes (132 calls, 0 failures, run in-process rather than over HTTP). A sweep of every GET for all 6 personas gave 774 valid responses, and trace replay shows 0 integrity failures on the seed.

## Broken on the real backend (`DATA_SOURCE=backend`, which is what `web/.env.local` is set to here)
1. **Trace replay gives false alarms.** In [handlers.ts:568](web/src/backend/handlers.ts:568) the replay gets no source records, so "every quote is found in its source" and "hashes match" fail for every signal, although the backend stores the records.
   - Audit events are passed newest-first, so the "no gaps" check fails too and the timeline is out of order.
   - "Score today" is computed over a single case with the mock formula, so it always reads rank 1 of 1.
2. **"New case by hand" fails.** The dialog sends an empty signal list ([case-forms.tsx:119](web/src/components/cases/case-forms.tsx:119)); the backend requires at least one, so it returns 422. Adding your own evidence returns 501.
3. **"Edit details" saves nothing but says "Details saved".** `patchCase` ([handlers.ts:423](web/src/backend/handlers.ts:423)) forwards only title, body, brand fit, rank, co-owners, watchers and scope. Short title, summary, car area, type and change depth are dropped. A requirement's change depth is also dropped, though the backend accepts it.
4. **Exports are not logged.** Codebeamer export, the deck and the case markdown are built in the adapter and never written to the audit trail; the mock logs all three.
5. **Signals page is truncated.** It loads at most 1,000 signals sorted by date, so the undated BMW verbatims drop out first. The backend's aggregate `/signals/flow` is unused.
6. **Competitor ripple is demo-only.** Refresh, ripples, and saving conversion factors or monitor settings return 501 or empty. The buttons still show, because the UI does not know which mode it is in.

## Conflicts with the project rules (both modes)
- **PM evidence counts as customers.** I added 30 PM notes to a hand-made case: it showed 30 customers and a customers factor of 0.84. The replay then showed two red integrity checks, because PM evidence has no source record.
- **Hand-made cases bypass the taxonomy.** They have no topic and a freely picked car area, while `CLAUDE.md` says the car area is always derived from the topic.
- **"Project type" is still in Settings.** It is a rejected option; on the backend it is ignored but still toasts "Workspace saved".

## Docs
`INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md` is stale: it says 56 endpoints, still lists `savePmContext`, and describes per-endpoint fallback to the mock, while `route.ts` now never mixes the two sources.

If the demo runs on mock data, none of the backend items block it. If it runs on real data, I would fix items 1 to 3 first; say so and I'll do it on a fresh branch off `origin/main`.
